direct.title: Dough preparation
direct.subtitle: Kneading and shaping
direct.step2Description: Mix yeast and honey with water
direct.step3Description: Add salt and flour and mix with wooden spoon
direct.step4Description: Once all ingredients are well mixed and you start to have a ball, you can place it on the work surface
direct.step5Description: Finish kneading by hand for about 10 min (you can use a stand mixer with its dough hook). Knead well to properly hydrate the flour
direct.step6Description: Once the dough has a nice structure, form a ball and let it rest for 25 min under a bowl (the dough will tighten and become smoother)
direct.step7Description: Perform some folds on the dough and give it a nice ball shape (smooth and no longer sticky)
direct.step8Description: Place the ball in an airtight container and let it rest for 24 hours
direct.step9Description: Retrieve the dough and, with a dough cutter or spatula, form dough balls (well stretched) of about { pizzaWeight } g
direct.step10Description: Place the dough balls in a dish leaving space between each (they will still grow)
direct.step11Description: Close the dish or cover it with plastic wrap and let rest for 3 hours

poolish.title: Poolish preparation
poolish.subtitle: First step: pre-fermentation preparation
poolish.step2Description: In a large bowl, dissolve the yeast in water and add honey
poolish.step3Description: Add flour and mix with a wooden spoon until you get a homogeneous mixture, then let rest { rtRestTime } hour(s) at room temperature covered with plastic wrap, then { coldRestTime } hour(s) in the refrigerator

dough.title: Dough preparation
dough.subtitle: Second step: kneading and shaping
dough.step2Description: Weigh the quantities to add to the poolish:
dough.step3Description: In the poolish bowl, add water and salt. Mix with spoon until water is absorbed
dough.step4Description: Add flour gradually and mix with spoon
dough.step5Description: When it's no longer possible to use a spoon, transfer dough to work surface
dough.step6Description: Work the dough by kneading it, the flour must be completely integrated
dough.step7Description: Make some folds with the dough and form a nice ball (soft and supple)
dough.step9Description: Reform a nice ball and let rest another 1H in an airtight container
dough.step10Description: Put a thin layer of fine semolina in a dish
dough.step11Description: Retrieve the dough and with a dough cutter or spatula form dough balls (well stretched) of about { pizzaWeight } g
dough.step12Description: Place the dough balls in the dish leaving space between them (they will still grow)
dough.step13Description: Close the dish or put plastic wrap on it and let rest between 1H & 3H
dough.tipsDescription: If the dough is too sticky, form a ball and let rest 10 min under a bowl
dough.successMessage: 🎉 And there you have it, they're ready to be transformed into PIZZA!

storage.title: Storage
storage.subtitle: Storage tips
storage.refrigerator: Refrigerator: Dough balls keep for 2-3 days
storage.freezer: Freezer: Freezes very well, don't keep more than 2-3 months
